nodes.label: Make It Ezy
nodes.rationale: Orchestration/discovery layer above the AI skill ecosystem; 'the intelligence is in choosing the right capabilities, not accumulating the most'. Should orchestrate the ecosystem, not replace it, and avoid becoming Ruflo #2.

nodes.label: EZ Agent System (router + 7 skills)
nodes.rationale: User was overwhelmed choosing among 25+ skills; reduce decision to one router plus a small set of specialized skills.

nodes.label: EZ Agent Router
nodes.rationale: Router decides which capability is needed so the developer need not remember which skill to invoke; must be conservative.

nodes.label: EZY Decision Engine
nodes.rationale: Heart of Make It Ezy: picks minimum set of capabilities/skills/agents/tools. Prefers one agent over swarms, existing skills over duplication, deterministic tools for calculations.

nodes.label: Project / Environment Analyzer
nodes.rationale: Understand repo before changes; avoid recommending what is already installed. First thing built (ezy analyze).

nodes.label: Capability Engine
nodes.rationale: System reasons about capabilities, not agents: converts a goal into required capabilities.

nodes.label: Skill Discovery
nodes.rationale: Search catalogs, evaluate license/compatibility/risk, recommend minimum useful set; never auto-install untrusted skills.

nodes.label: Live External Skill Registry
nodes.rationale: Copying external skills means re-patching when upstream changes; instead track source/version/commit/content hash like an app store, not a warehouse.

nodes.label: Specialist
nodes.rationale: Logical domain role (e.g. Video Editor, Structural Engineer); not necessarily a separate model or agent.

nodes.label: Skill
nodes.rationale: Reusable instructions/methodology/domain knowledge.

nodes.label: Tool
nodes.rationale: Something that lets an agent act (FFmpeg, browser, MCP).

nodes.label: Specialist/Capability/Skill/Tool/Workflow/Runtime/Provider Terminology
nodes.rationale: Stop calling everything a skill; structural engineering example showed need for risk-aware capability model.

nodes.label: Risk and Permission System
nodes.rationale: High-risk domains (structural engineering, medical, legal, security) require independent verification and human professional review; never present AI output as licensed approval.

nodes.label: Runtime / Execution Adapter
nodes.rationale: Hides per-runtime differences in installing skills, loading instructions, invoking tools; avoids hard-coding around Claude Code.

nodes.label: Verification Layer
nodes.rationale: Never claim done/tests passed without running them; outcomes SUCCESS/PARTIAL/FAILED/REQUIRES HUMAN REVIEW.

nodes.label: Ponytail Principle (Simplify Before Expanding)
nodes.rationale: Cross-cutting constraint, not a stage: minimum unnecessary complexity, not minimum code.

nodes.label: No AI Bureaucracy Rule
nodes.rationale: Avoid router->planner->reviewer->reviewer-reviewer chains; smart enough to help, simple enough to understand.

nodes.label: Local-First Memory Separation
nodes.rationale: Separate session/project/workflow memory, skill registry cache, agent history; start with SQLite/JSON/filesystem/Git, no vector DB without demonstrated need.

nodes.label: Free Core + BYOK Cost Philosophy
nodes.rationale: A hosted site paying for users' tokens is financially brutal; core is free/open-source/local-first, users bring their own model, Claude Code subscription, or Ollama.

nodes.label: Future Local AI Workstation Spec
nodes.rationale: Prioritize 16-24+ GB VRAM; 64-128 GB RAM, 2-4 TB NVMe. Software must scale from 16GB laptop without rewrite.

nodes.label: ezy analyze
nodes.rationale: First vertical slice; no AI required.

nodes.label: Phase 0-6 Roadmap
nodes.rationale: Each phase earns the next: research, tiny CLI, discovery, decision engine, install+adapters, verification+memory, web UI. Tell Codex to do Phase 0 and 1 only.

nodes.label: TypeScript + Node.js + pnpm Stack Decision
nodes.rationale: Make It Ezy lives in a Node-heavy ecosystem (npm, npx, MCP, SKILL.md, Claude Code/Codex/Cursor) and matches owner's experience; earlier Python recommendation reversed. No framework, DB or web UI initially.

nodes.label: Python Core Option (uv + Typer + Pydantic)
nodes.rationale: Briefly recommended for inspection/orchestration work, later superseded by TypeScript.

nodes.label: Artifact Data Model
nodes.rationale: Artifact subtypes Skill/Workflow/Tool/Runtime/Capability Provider with source, version, license, permissions, trust, evidence.

nodes.label: Security as Cross-Cutting Concern
nodes.rationale: Security spans discovery (provenance), installation (scripts/deps), execution (commands/secrets/network).

nodes.label: AI Capability Discovery & Orchestration Tool (vs Package Manager)
nodes.rationale: A package manager answers where/how to install; Make It Ezy answers what to use at all, using npm/pnpm underneath.

nodes.label: Use Skills to Build Make It Ezy
nodes.rationale: Superpowers helps build Make It Ezy; Agent Skills defines what it should understand; specialized skills become discoverable examples.

nodes.label: Video Research Inventory Process
nodes.rationale: Collect tools from videos as Study items first, evaluate later to avoid premature adoption.

nodes.label: Agent Skills Standard Compatibility (no proprietary format)
nodes.rationale: Understand existing SKILL.md format rather than invent a Make It Ezy skill framework.
